newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: French yachtsman safe, Briton still missing.
newsitem.headline: French yachtsman safe, Briton still missing.

text.p: Australian rescue officials found missing French yachtsman Thierry Dubois in the Southern Ocean on Monday but there was no sign of life on a second yacht belonging to Britain's Tony Bullimore.

Dubois climbed aboard a raft dropped by rescue planes at 6 p.m. local time (1000 GMT), about 1,400 nautical miles southwest of Perth, Australian Defence Force spokesman Colonel Andrew Reynolds told Reuters.
Rescue planes found Bullimore's listing yacht west of Dubois' position but there was no sign of whether the other round-the-world sailor was still aboard.
"(Bullimore's) yacht is listing and there is no sign of life on board, but that is not to say that he isn't there because he could be below deck," Reynolds said.
"We have marked his position and will be back there at first light with another Orion (search plane)," he said.
Bullimore, 56, on board Global Exide Challenger, and 29-year-old Dubois on board Amnesty International sent out distress calls late on Sunday after sailing into a storm.

The two competitors in the Vendee Globe round-the-world race hit difficulties about 120 nautical miles south of the region where French yachtsman Raphael Dinelli was rescued from his sinking yacht two days after Christmas.
Reynolds said two planes had been involved in finding Dubois and Bullimore's yacht.
The first raft Dubois had climbed aboard capsized but he later managed to climb aboard another raft dropped by the second rescue plane.
"He had a bit of an adventure getting there, but he is safely on board," Reynolds said.
"We have also dropped a communication package and hope to be in communication with him tomorrow morning."
Weather conditions deteriorated during the day with a heavy swell of six metres and winds of 40-50 knots, ahead of an expected storm.
Dubois now faces up to three days in the raft before he was picked up by the Royal Australian Navy frigate HMAS Adelaide, which left Perth on Monday equipped with a Seahawk helicopter.
Reynolds said there were no commercial boats or other Vendee Globe competitors in the area who could divert to the scene.
Dubois' capsized and partly submerged yacht was first located shortly after 1 p.m. local time (0500 GMT) with the Frenchman clinging to the hull.
Rescue officials did not know which of the two yachtsmen they had found until Dubois climbed aboard the second raft about five hours later.
The rescue mission was the longest rescue Australian authorities had attempted for yachtsmen, Australian Maritime Safety Authority spokesman David Gray said.
Two years ago Australian officials launched a large-scale rescue mission to save French yachtswoman Isabelle Autissier, who was competing in the BOC Round-the-World Yacht race.
